label: Port-au-Prince City Center
sub: Haiti's capital and most conflict-affected urban zone. UN BINUH estimates gang control at approximately 90% of the city as of March 2026; PM Fils-Aimé claimed a reduction to ~75% on May 1, 2026, citing early GSF joint operations — the first government claim of rollback since 2021. The National Palace and key government buildings remain in a narrow government-held corridor.

label: Cité Soleil
sub: Densely populated waterfront commune entirely controlled by rival gang factions. Site of the July 2022 G9 vs. G-Pèp massacre (207 dead) and December 2024 Wharf Jérémie massacre (207 dead). Home to over 300,000 people in extreme poverty. On May 10–12, 2026, intense gang fighting triggered the evacuation of MSF's hospital — the only health facility accessible to the commune — and the suspension of the Centre Hospitalier de Fontaine, forcing the evacuation of 11 newborns. MSF treated 40+ gunshot victims before evacuating; 800+ displaced civilians sheltered inside the compound before it closed.

label: MSF Cité Soleil Hospital (Emergency Dept Reopened Jun 1)
sub: MSF's hospital in Cité Soleil — the only health facility accessible to the commune's ~300,000 residents living under total gang control. On May 10, 2026, intense gang fighting forced MSF to evacuate the facility and temporarily suspend all services after treating 40+ gunshot victims in 12 hours. 800+ displaced civilians had sheltered inside the compound. One MSF security guard was shot. After 25 days of forced closure, MSF announced the emergency department and sexual violence survivor care unit at Cité Soleil were operational again as of June 1, 2026 — confirmed active on June 4. This was the third time in three years MSF was forced to suspend Cité Soleil operations. Outpatient and full inpatient services are expected to resume in phases contingent on continued relative security. The GSF advance force of ~800 personnel remains concentrated in the city center corridor with no coverage of Cité Soleil, meaning the hospital's fragile operational status depends on an uneasy inter-gang ceasefire rather than sustained security.

label: Village de Dieu (PNH Offensive, Jun 1–ongoing)
sub: Densely populated neighborhood in southwest Port-au-Prince along Route Nationale 2 (RN2), controlled for over five years by the 'Baz 5 Segonn' (5 Seconds) gang. On June 1, 2026, the Haitian National Police launched the largest security operation in the RN2 corridor in years — deploying armored vehicles, explosive drones, and tear gas. By June 4, at least 6 firearms were seized and several gang members killed; the PNH deliberately destroyed a malfunctioning armored vehicle to deny it to the gang. June 5: PNH issued a public safety warning that gangs are using civilians as human shields. June 6+: Operation continues into at least Day 6 as of the June 6 news cycle. Strategic objective: reopen RN2 to civilian traffic, restoring the critical supply corridor to Haiti's southern peninsula severed since 2021. The offensive marks the first sustained police presence in Village de Dieu in over five years and represents the most significant PNH counter-gang operation of 2026.

label: Cul-de-Sac Plain (May 2026 Intra-Viv Ansanm Clashes)
sub: Peri-urban eastern corridor supplying Port-au-Prince with cargo from the Dominican Republic. On May 10–12, 2026, intra-Viv Ansanm gang fighting erupted between Duvivier/Pyè 6 factions and Chen Mechan/Taliban/400 Mawozo groups from Croix-des-Missions and Canaan. At least 8 killed, hundreds to ~5,000 displaced. Gangs contest extortion of cargo trucks using this corridor. The clashes reflect fragmentation of the Viv Ansanm coalition as GSF operations disrupt established revenue networks in central Port-au-Prince.

label: Wharf Jérémie (Dec 2024 Massacre)
sub: Site of the December 6–11, 2024 massacre in which gang leader Micanor Altes killed 207 confirmed civilians, including elderly Vodou practitioners. Bodies were burned and thrown into the sea. UN designated it an atrocity.

label: Varreux Fuel Terminal
sub: Haiti's main petroleum import terminal, supplying ~70% of national fuel. Blockaded by G9 gangs in October 2021 and again in September 2022, triggering humanitarian crises in hospitals and water systems. Recaptured by MSS in 2024.

label: Toussaint Louverture Intl Airport
sub: Haiti's main international airport. Attacked by gangs on March 4, 2024, forcing a months-long closure. MSS forces secured the perimeter in mid-2024, enabling flight resumption. April 20, 2026: gang clashes in Plaine du Cul-de-Sac (Chen Mechan vs. Duvivier/Pyè 6 factions) sent gunfire to the airport perimeter, striking a terminal window and forcing Sunrise Airways to suspend flights for the day. The FAA maintains a flight ban over Port-au-Prince through September 2026.

label: National Palace
sub: Haiti's presidential palace and seat of government. Damaged in the 2010 earthquake. Site where the Transitional Presidential Council was sworn in on April 25, 2024. Lies in a narrow government-controlled corridor within Port-au-Prince.

label: Hôpital de l'Université d'État d'Haïti (HUEH)
sub: Haiti's main public hospital, repeatedly threatened by gang violence. Faced critical fuel shortages during 2021 and 2022 terminal blockades. MSS forces helped secure its perimeter in 2024 but the facility remains severely understaffed and underfunded.

label: Bel Air (Gang Zone)
sub: Urban neighborhood in northern Port-au-Prince controlled by G9-affiliated gangs. Key node in the gang corridor linking Cité Soleil to the city center. Site of the 2018 La Saline massacre and ongoing gang operations.

label: La Saline
sub: Waterfront slum and gang stronghold. Site of the 2018 La Saline massacre (71 killed) under G9 affiliated groups. Remains under gang control and serves as a gateway to port facilities and Varreux terminal.

label: Martissant
sub: Chokepoint neighborhood on Route Nationale 2, the only road connecting Port-au-Prince to Haiti's southern peninsula. Gang control effectively severed the south from the capital since 2021. MSF was forced to suspend its emergency hospital operations here repeatedly.

label: Delmas
sub: Sprawling middle-class district increasingly affected by gang expansion from the north and west. Multiple police stations have been attacked. Significant IDP population sheltered in local schools and churches since 2022.

label: Pétion-Ville
sub: Affluent hillside suburb and diplomatic hub where the Montana Accord was formed in August 2021. Home to international NGOs, embassies, and upper-middle-class residents. Increasingly targeted by kidnappers despite historically lower violence levels.

label: Tabarre IDP Sites
sub: Area northeast of Port-au-Prince hosting multiple IDP displacement sites since 2022. Thousands of families displaced from Cité Soleil, Martissant, and other gang-controlled areas. Sites face severe overcrowding, lack of sanitation, and cholera risk.

label: Croix-des-Bouquets National Penitentiary
sub: Site of a coordinated gang prison break on March 2, 2024, which freed approximately 2,000 inmates. The warden was killed in the assault. The breakout formed part of Viv Ansanm's broader February–March 2024 offensive that precipitated PM Henry's departure.

label: Port-au-Prince Civil Prison
sub: Haiti's main civil detention facility, stormed by gang forces on March 3, 2024, freeing approximately 2,700 inmates. The coordinated prison breaks—alongside the airport attack—marked the peak of Viv Ansanm's offensive that ousted PM Henry.

label: MSS / GSF Forward Operating Base
sub: Primary forward operating base fully transitioned to Gang Suppression Force (GSF) use as of April 28, 2026, when the final 150 Kenyan MSS officers departed. As of May 14, 2026, commanded by Mongolian Maj. Gen. Erdenebat Batsuuri — the first non-Kenyan commander of an international security mission in Haiti. The GSF advance contingent (~800 personnel: 400+ Chadian, 75 Guatemalan, 70 Salvadoran) coordinates joint operations with the Haitian National Police from this location. Force remains concentrated in Port-au-Prince city center; Cité Soleil and the Artibonite have no GSF coverage.

label: Kenyan MSS Operational Hub
sub: Former coordination hub for Kenyan National Police Service officers deployed under the MSS mandate. Kenya's final 150 officers departed Haiti on April 28, 2026, formally ending the 22-month MSS mission. First Kenyan officer killed in combat, Samuel Tompei Kaetuai, was based at this facility before his death on February 24, 2025. Now transitioning to GSF support functions.

label: UN BINUH Office
sub: Headquarters of the United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH), mandated to support political stability and human rights monitoring. Repeatedly reported on gang violence, IDP conditions, and government failures. Mandate extended through 2026.

label: Cap-Haïtien
sub: Haiti's second-largest city in the north. Historically more stable than Port-au-Prince but increasingly affected by gang expansion in 2024–2025. Cap-Haïtien airport served as an alternate MSS supply entry point. In May 2026, the Dominican Republic reopened its airspace to Cap-Haïtien after approximately two years of suspension — a modest positive for northern Haiti's connectivity and economic activity.

label: Les Cayes
sub: Southern Haiti's main city, devastated by the August 14, 2021, 7.2 magnitude earthquake that killed 2,200+ people. MSF and international NGOs established field hospitals here. The Martissant gang blockade isolated this region from Port-au-Prince aid for extended periods.

label: Jacmel
sub: Southern coastal city and cultural hub. Affected by the 2021 earthquake and the Martissant corridor blockade that periodically severed road access from the capital. Jacmel's port serves as an alternative supply route for the region's 600,000+ residents.

label: Jérémie
sub: Capital of the Grand'Anse department on Haiti's southern peninsula. Heavily damaged by the 2021 earthquake and isolated by the Martissant blockade. Receives humanitarian supplies primarily by sea and air when road access is cut.

label: Gonaïves
sub: Capital of the Artibonite Department and Haiti's third-largest city. Located on Route Nationale 1, the main artery to the north. Gang expansion into the Artibonite Valley in 2024–2025 threatened access to this historically significant 'City of Independence.'

label: Pont-Sondé (Oct 2024 Massacre)
sub: Town in the Artibonite Department attacked by the Gran Grif gang on October 3, 2024. At least 115 civilians killed, including infants and elderly, when gunmen arrived by canoe. Over 6,270 residents fled. The attack demonstrated the spread of gang violence beyond Port-au-Prince.

label: Saint-Marc
sub: Strategic port city in Artibonite, gateway to the Artibonite Valley rice-growing region. Gang expansion in 2024–2025 threatened the area's agricultural economy. A key transit point on Route Nationale 1 where gangs have established checkpoints and extortion operations. On May 5, 2026, municipal authorities imposed a nightly curfew banning vehicle and motorcycle traffic from 8:30 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. due to deteriorating security conditions driven by the spread of gang activity from deeper in the Artibonite Valley following Gran Grif's March–April 2026 offensive.

label: Hinche
sub: Capital of the Centre Department, an historically quiet agricultural region. Gang expansion from Port-au-Prince reached Centre in 2024–2025, with BINUH reports noting violence flaring in communities along the Route du Centre.

label: Port-de-Paix
sub: Capital of the Northwest Department. Gang activities in the northwest escalated in 2025 as Viv Ansanm extended influence along routes toward the Dominican border. The region had limited MSS presence.

label: Miragoâne
sub: Southern port city in Nippes Department. Key entry point for humanitarian supplies into the south after the Martissant blockade closed Route Nationale 2. MSF operated medical facilities in the region serving earthquake-affected and displaced populations.

label: Arcahaie
sub: Coastal town on Route Nationale 1 north of Port-au-Prince. Gang-controlled checkpoints in the Arcahaie area effectively tax or block cargo trucks heading to the capital, contributing to supply shortages. Agricultural produce from northern Haiti must pass through this corridor.

label: Canaan / Jerusalem IDP Zone
sub: Massive informal settlement northeast of Port-au-Prince, home to hundreds of thousands who fled the 2010 earthquake and never returned. Serves as a receiving area for new IDP waves from gang violence in 2021–2025. Limited services, high disease burden, and cholera outbreaks.

label: Champ de Mars IDP Sites
sub: Public spaces around the National Palace converted to IDP shelters. Thousands of families displaced from gang-controlled zones live in makeshift camps with minimal sanitation. UN reports document cholera cases and sexual violence targeting displaced women and girls.

label: MSF Tabarre Emergency Hospital
sub: MSF trauma hospital in Tabarre, one of the few facilities able to treat gunshot and machete wounds during Port-au-Prince gang violence. Faced critical fuel shortages during 2022 Varreux blockades. Performs hundreds of complex surgical procedures monthly.

label: MSF Martissant Emergency Centre
sub: MSF emergency and trauma center in Martissant, the gang-controlled chokepoint on Route Nationale 2. The facility was forced to suspend operations multiple times between 2021–2025 due to direct armed attacks, sniper fire, and gang incursions. Thousands of patients lost access to emergency care.

label: OCHA Haiti Coordination Hub
sub: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs hub managing Haiti's humanitarian response. Coordinates between 200+ NGOs and UN agencies. Issues regular situation reports on IDP numbers, food insecurity, cholera, and humanitarian access constraints.

label: Carrefour
sub: Large suburban commune west of Port-au-Prince along the coast. Heavy gang presence with multiple armed groups competing for control. Carrefour lies on the western approach to Route Nationale 2 and is a key node in the gang stranglehold on southern Haiti.

label: Léogâne
sub: Coastal town that suffered extensive damage in the 2010 earthquake. Since 2021, gang activity on Route Nationale 2 has periodically cut off humanitarian access. The town serves as a reference point for WHO cholera monitoring in the southern corridor.

label: Pelerin 5 (Moïse Assassination Site)
sub: Hillside neighborhood of Pétion-Ville where President Jovenel Moïse was assassinated at his private residence on July 7, 2021. The attack was carried out by a team of 28 mercenaries, mostly Colombian nationals. The site became a focal point for investigations and political controversy.

label: Artibonite Valley (Agricultural Zone)
sub: Haiti's most important rice-growing region, feeding millions. Gang expansion by Gran Grif and other groups in 2023–2025 disrupted planting seasons, extorted farmers, and forced displacement. Loss of Artibonite production dramatically worsened food insecurity.

label: Jean-Denis (Mar 2026 Massacre)
sub: Site of the March 30, 2026 Gran Grif gang massacre near Pont-Sondé. Pre-dawn attack killed at least 16 confirmed (up to 70 per RNDDH) and wounded ~30 civilians, displacing nearly 6,000 residents. Gran Grif retaliated against the community following an assault on its base in Savien by a rival group. Attack echoed the October 2024 Pont-Sondé massacre by the same gang.

label: Seguin/Marigot — Sud-Est Gang Expansion (Apr–May 2026)
sub: Gang attacks in Seguin, Marigot commune (Sud-Est department) on April 13–14, 2026, killed at least 7–8 people and displaced 4,000+ residents — the first gang-driven displacement at this scale recorded in the historically low-violence Sud-Est department. Attackers burned the local police sub-station and vehicles. Attributed to Viv Ansanm-affiliated groups. Protests shut down Jacmel on April 15–16. Haiti's Anti-Gang Tactical Unit (UTAG) deployed as reinforcements. By May 2026, ACLED documented a record 38 deaths in the Sud-Est department — including in Macary and Seguin — as gang violence spread beyond Port-au-Prince and the Artibonite. ACLED analysts assess this as a 'balloon effect' of GSF/HNP pressure in the capital displacing gang factions to regions with weaker institutional presence.

label: Kenscoff (May 2026 Gang Attack)
sub: Mountainous community above Pétion-Ville, historically a relative refuge for Haitians displaced from Port-au-Prince's gang-controlled lowlands. On May 4, 2026, a gang attack was reported in the Malong area of Kenscoff — signaling continued expansion of Viv Ansanm-affiliated armed groups into hillside communities that had previously been beyond gang reach. Kenscoff's altitude and narrow mountain roads had slowed gang penetration, making this incident a significant indicator of widening territorial control.

label: Kafou Robert (May 2026 Gang Attack)
sub: Community in the fourth section of Saint-Marc, Artibonite Department. On May 9, 2026, armed members of the Savien gang killed 8 residents and wounded 3 in a direct attack on the community, occurring while PM Fils-Aimé was in Rome. The attack took place despite Saint-Marc's May 5 curfew and with no GSF presence in the Artibonite. Savien gang is part of the Viv Ansanm coalition consolidating Route Nationale 1.

label: Fort-Liberté
sub: Capital of the Northeast Department, near the Dominican border. As gangs expanded northward along Route Nationale 6 in 2025, Fort-Liberté became a point of concern for cross-border trafficking and gang movement toward the Dominican frontier.

label: Haitian National Police (PNH) HQ
sub: Headquarters of the Haitian National Police, which had an estimated active force of 15,000–17,000 officers in a country of 12 million. Heavily infiltrated by gang informants, under-equipped, and frequently outgunned. Multiple police stations were seized during the February–March 2024 gang offensive.

label: Kenyan Embassy / MSS Liaison
sub: Kenyan diplomatic mission in Port-au-Prince serving as a key administrative liaison for the MSS deployment. The embassy managed bilateral coordination between the Haitian Transitional Council and the Kenyan National Police Service command.

label: Artibonite Cholera Cluster
sub: The Artibonite region was one of the original epicenters of the UN-linked cholera outbreak that began in 2010. The 2022 resurgence also started here. Gangs control water infrastructure and block public health responses, allowing cholera to spread through displacement camps and unprotected water sources.

label: UN Support Office in Haiti (UNSOH)
sub: Headquarters of the newly established United Nations Support Office in Haiti (UNSOH), created to provide logistics, intelligence sharing, and operational support to the Gang Suppression Force (GSF). Daniela Kroslak appointed as UNSOH head in March 2026. Replaces prior MSS logistics coordination functions.

label: Marchand Dessalines (Gran Grif Advance, Apr 2026)
sub: Strategic Artibonite town targeted by Gran Grif and Kokorat San Ras gangs following the March 30, 2026 Jean-Denis massacre. Gang members filmed distributing cash to residents — a control tactic — as forces advanced ~19 km north of the massacre site. On May 7, 2026, Viv Ansanm gang coalition destroyed the Marchand-Dessalines police station in a direct assault on state security infrastructure; Haitian security forces launched anti-terrorist 'Operation Viv Ansanm' in response, killing 10+ gang members. The police station destruction signals Viv Ansanm's move to consolidate control along Route Nationale 1 beyond Port-au-Prince.

label: Mirebalais (University Hospital — Closed)
sub: The University Hospital in Mirebalais, Centre Department, was shuttered due to gang violence expanding into the Centre Department in 2024–2025. The facility previously served 185,000 patients. Its closure — one of several hospital shutdowns across Haiti — contributed to an acute healthcare access crisis as gangs expanded beyond Port-au-Prince.

label: Citadelle Laferrière (Apr 2026 Stampede)
sub: UNESCO World Heritage mountaintop fortress near Milot, Nord Department. Site of a deadly stampede on April 11–12, 2026, in which at least 30 people were killed during a youth tourist activity. Panic reportedly triggered by police tear gas and worsened by rain on steep mountainside approaches. Site closed indefinitely. The Citadelle, completed in 1820, is Haiti's most iconic national monument.

label: Shalom Church IDP Site (Delmas 33, May 2026)
sub: Evangelical church in the Delmas 33 neighborhood of Port-au-Prince that became an emergency displacement shelter during the May 2026 Cité Soleil violence surge. UN News (May 20, 2026) reported the Shalom Church was hosting more than 2,000 newly displaced persons after gang-set fires in Cité Soleil and the Cul-de-Sac Plain drove 30,000+ from their homes since May 10. WFP Port-au-Prince field office head Janvier Muhima cited the site as emblematic of the humanitarian emergency. WFP reached 8,500 newly displaced with emergency food during this period; nine nearby WFP-supported schools serving ~12,000 students were forced to suspend meal distributions.

label: Nan Brooklyn / Chancerelles Gang Offensive (May 26–27, 2026)
sub: On May 26–27, 2026, gang forces launched a two-day offensive in the Nan Brooklyn neighborhood of central Port-au-Prince, killing 4 people, injuring 20, and burning homes. Witnesses alleged police armored vehicles were used by gang leader Jimmy Chérizier ('Barbecue') in the approach — allegations denied or unanswered by HNP. By May 27, gang forces had installed new leadership in Chancerelles, Nan Tokyo, Nan Barozi, Delmas 2, and Delmas 4 — a consolidation of the gang territorial perimeter immediately adjacent to the narrow government-controlled city center corridor. The offensive follows the May 25 Krache Dife IDP camp attack in Delmas 6 and the May 10–14 Cité Soleil/Cul-de-Sac violence wave, and contradicts PM Fils-Aimé's May 1 claim of gang territory rolling back to ~75%.

label: Krache Dife IDP Camp Attack — Delmas 6 (May 25, 2026)
sub: On May 25, 2026, Krache Dife de Delmas 6 gang — a Viv Ansanm coalition faction — attacked a displaced persons camp in the Delmas 6 corridor, killing 2 people including a minor and burning 24 houses. The attack represents a documented gang tactic of targeting IDP camps to assert territorial control over humanitarian spaces and generate secondary displacement. As approximately 1.5 million Haitians remain internally displaced nationwide, attacks on displacement sites compound an already critical humanitarian emergency. The GSF's ~800-person advance force has no coverage in the Delmas zone, leaving IDP camps there entirely dependent on the severely understaffed Haitian National Police.

label: Petite Rivière de Bayonnais (1,100+ Displaced, May–Jun 2026)
sub: Town in Artibonite Department where gang violence on May 26, 2026 displaced more than 1,100 people who fled northward to Gonaïves seeking safety. Documented in IOM Emergency Tracking Tool Report 95 (May 29 – June 1, 2026). UN spokesman Stéphane Dujarric confirmed ongoing armed attacks driving Artibonite displacement on June 1. The Artibonite has zero GSF coverage as of June 2, 2026 — no deployment timeline announced. Part of the Gran Grif gang expansion pattern following the October 2024 Pont-Sondé massacre and March 2026 Jean-Denis attack.

label: Kenscoff Massacre (61 Killed, Jul 7-9, 2026)
sub: Multi-day gang assault on Kenscoff's Roben locality beginning the night of July 7-8, 2026, killing at least 61 people including 14 children and burning most houses in the affected localities. IOM recorded 5,840 people (1,836 households) displaced (ETT 100.1, Jul 4-9). OHCHR/BINUH issued a flash report. One month later, on August 7, Village-de-Dieu gang members attacked police reinforcements sent to the commune, torching a PNH armored vehicle.

label: Gros-Mornes Massacre (Artibonite, Aug 7-8, 2026)
sub: The Kokorat San Ras gang attacked Gros-Mornes in Artibonite over the weekend of August 7-8, 2026, killing at least a dozen people per residents and the town's mayor. Artibonite accounts for 381 fatalities (25.7% of the national 2026 year-to-date total) — the second-most affected department nationally — with negligible GSF or PNH coverage.

label: Arcahaie Attack by Canaan 'Taliban' Gang (Aug 9, 2026)
sub: The 'Taliban' gang, based in the Canaan informal settlement north of Port-au-Prince, attacked the coastal town of Arcahaie on August 9, 2026, roughly 30 miles north of the capital, killing at least one truck driver — extending gang reach further along the Route Nationale 1 northern corridor.

label: Ganthier Armed Clashes (1,300+ Displaced, Jul 1, 2026)
sub: Armed clashes on July 1, 2026 in Ganthier's Pinso and Grand-État localities (Mare Roseaux, West Department) displaced approximately 1,328 people (262 households), per IOM ETT 99 (Jul 1-7). All displaced found shelter with host families within Ganthier, near the Dominican Republic border corridor.

label: Marmont Paul Attack — Saint-Michel-de-l'Atalaye (Aug 18, 2026)
sub: Kokorat San Ras and Gran Grif gang members attacked the Marmont Paul locality in Saint-Michel-de-l'Atalaye's 7th communal section, Artibonite, HaitiLibre reported August 18, 2026, killing at least one person, wounding several others, and burning homes — the latest in a string of Kokorat San Ras/Gran Grif attacks in Artibonite following the August 7-8 Gros-Mornes massacre.

label: Kenscoff Church Massacre & Accountability Crisis (47 Killed, 50+ Kidnapped, Aug 23-27, 2026)
sub: Viv Ansanm coalition gunmen — led locally by Johnson 'Izo 2' André's 5 Segonn faction — stormed Kenscoff on the night of August 23, 2026, torching roughly 25 homes and executing people, including children, inside a church sheltering people already displaced by earlier violence. The UN confirmed on August 26 that the toll had risen to at least 47 killed (5+ children) and more than 50 kidnapped, with 22 victims executed inside the church compound per BINUH; IOM recorded 2,647 displaced. A gang leader posted a hostage video threatening to kill captives if security forces pursued gang members. PNH opened an internal investigation Aug 24; by Aug 27 residents demanded the local police chief's resignation, Amnesty International demanded accountability, and a gang leader threatened to attack Tabarre (US embassy neighborhood). This is the second major Kenscoff massacre in under two months, following the 61-killed attack of July 7-9, 2026.
